Root cause was broader than reported: three nested retry layers with none owning reconnection. The reported schedule defects (whileOutput terminating instead of clamping, upTo(5min) counting healthy uptime, one retry driver spanning the fiber lifetime, silent exhaustion with running=true) were real and are fixed, but they were only 1 of 3 silent failure modes. The most common - a transport error - never reached that code at all: the OpenCode SDK's own SSE loop swallows errors and retries internally forever, so conduit's for-await just blocked with connected=true, no disconnect broadcast, no permission resync, and isConnected() reporting healthy so pollers never started either.

Fixed in 5fba3572 on fix/c4z-lifecycle-queue-deadlock.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, then reproduced deterministically): enqueueLifecycleEffect built an Effect.async with NO interruption canceler. An interrupted caller left resume inert, so the work effect and its Effect.ensuring(release) never ran, completion never settled, and lifecycleQueue was permanently pending - hanging every later connect/disconnect/drain including the shutdown finalizer at sse-stream-service.ts:24.

FIX: return Effect.sync(release) as the canceler. One statement.

MUTUAL EXCLUSION VERIFIED, and my initial reasoning was WRONG in two places (corrected by the adversarial review against effect 3.21.2 source + two runtime probes): (a) the canceler CAN fire after resume - the resumed work stays inside the async node's onInterrupt continuation; it is safe instead because ensuring brackets its finalizer uninterruptibly and continuations unwind inside-out, so the inner release always precedes the outer and the work has already terminated; (b) Effect.uninterruptible around startConnectionEffect does not lexically wrap the canceler - it defers it indirectly because an interrupt received while masked is only acted on when interruptibility is restored. Probe output: [registered, inner ensuring, outer canceler].

TESTS - two complementary cases, and note carefully which guards what. 'does not poison the lifecycle queue when a queued caller is interrupted' FAILS without the fix (drain times out) - this is the c4z regression test. 'continues the lifecycle queue when the active caller is interrupted' PASSES without the canceler by design, because that path releases via the work's own inner ensuring; it instead guards that queued work cannot start early. I verified this by removing the canceler and running both, rather than accepting the implementing agent's mutation claim.

NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: directly interrupting a queued disconnect/drain still skips its cleanup (running=false, abort(), Fiber.interrupt) and can leave an SSE fiber alive until a later disconnect. Pre-existing, not expanded by this change, and production shutdown is unaffected because Effect installs scope finalizers with interruption disabled (fiberRuntime.ts:1710-1730). Do NOT claim direct disconnect/drain is cancellation-safe.

WHAT SHIPPED, vs what the ticket originally asked for: the ticket offered two options -- tolerate provider 404 as success, or reorder with compensation. It shipped as neither. The tombstone commits first and provider cleanup is best-effort afterwards, which deletes the 404 special-case entirely rather than implementing it.

BIGGER THAN HARDENING. The ticket called this hardening, not a regression. That was wrong: deleteSession's failure aborted the whole downstream sequence in handlers/session.ts (no tombstone, no local state cleanup, no daemon publish, no session_deleted broadcast, no session lists, no success log; RPC returned an error). So this is the change that makes deletion work end to end.

THREE THINGS FOUND DURING THE WORK THAT THE TICKET DID NOT ANTICIPATE:

1. Tombstone-first alone would have SILENTLY BROKEN cleanup on the restart path. The session.deleted projector deletes session_providers, which is where the engine resolves end_session's route. A session bound in the current process survives via the in-memory transient overlay, but one bound before a daemon restart has only the durable row -- and handleEndSessionEffect treats an absent binding as a SUCCESSFUL no-op. Cleanup would have been skipped with no receipt, and no force-the-failure test would have caught it. Fixed by capturing the route before the tombstone.

2. The first implementation routed cleanup by temporarily RE-BINDING the session into the shared engine. Review proved the window is reachable (handlers/model.ts:647 binds without checking sessions; provider-turn-service.ts:687 explicitly continues when getSession returns no row, then binds at :623; orchestration-engine.ts:451 binds an accepted durable turn) and that unbindSession was not ownership-aware -- it wrote sessionId -> null, masking whatever binding it found. Replaced with an optional targetProviderId on EndSessionCommand plus revision-aware compare-and-swap unbinding in ProviderSessionBindingReadModel, so cleanup clears only a binding it still owns. This also fixes the same latent clobber on the engine's own unbind path.

3. The diagnostic path could break the delete it was reporting on: formatErrorDetail JSON.stringify's arbitrary provider responseBody, so a circular object, BigInt or throwing getter would throw a defect that escaped AFTER the tombstone, killing publishSessionDeleted and the broadcast. Now rendered through a total renderer that cannot throw, and length-bounded (2000 per detail, 4000 aggregate) so a large provider body cannot become a large durable event.

Cleanup is bounded at 2s (user decision) because the handler's broadcast waits on it; a timeout is recorded like any other cleanup failure. Receipt is event-store-and-log only, per user decision -- no projector arm, no migration, nothing browser-facing.

Fixed on wt/foreman-j0a commit 2d8cc2e3 (foreman-auto ni818). Removed per-session revision reuse entirely rather than pruning: transient bindings use a read-model-instance-wide monotonic generator whose token is deleted with the binding, and durable-only bindings allocate NO map entry at all -- their generation derives from the active session_providers row's own (id, activated_at) composite identity. Map is now bounded by live bindings, not lifetime totals. Pruning was proven unsafe: unbindSessionIfBoundTo runs as an Effect.ensuring finalizer in the dispatching fiber and overlapping deletes are not deduplicated, so concurrent stale finalizers per session have no code-defined maximum -- no LRU or TTL can be proven safe. Generator is never reset (see conduit-test-gja). Row id ALONE was insufficient (deterministic ids can be reused with a newer activated_at); a test covers that. Cross-model review found 2 real defects in the first attempt (stale CAS could still clobber via the durable path; durable-only tokens orphaned on DB-side deletion, i.e. the ticket's own bug was unfixed for SQLite) -- both fixed in a delta pass. Fixed on wt/foreman-pfh commit fb2bd514 (foreman-auto ni818). Provider ownership is now established synchronously before a session is exposed: default create, named create and fork children append+project a canonical session.created plus their initial binding before any broadcast, and VERIFY the projected row and active binding exist afterwards (projectEvent records individual projector failures and returns success, so it could not serve as a fail-closed boundary alone). Failed establishment removes its seed row rather than leaving a session later exposed by SQL-backed session lists. Claude persistence no longer establishes sessions it did not create -- a missing lifecycle is a typed error, gated on a canonical creation event or active binding rather than mere row presence -- and a lifecycle rejection now FAILS the turn instead of logging and dispatching anyway (which had let Claude execute tools and modify files with no durable prompt explaining them). Ingress dedups creation against the PROJECTED SESSION ROW, not event-log history; keying on the log killed re-seed self-healing after a transient projection failure. Fail-closed applies only where persistence is configured (persistenceDbPath is optional and addProjectRelay builds stacks without it -- see conduit-test-02h). Neither projector twin changed; provider = excluded.provider not restored. Full pnpm test:unit green from the parent: 472 files, 6181 tests. Three passes were needed: the first broke 5 pre-existing tests (codex cannot run the socket-bound suite) and a cross-model review found 5 further defects (4xP1). Fixed on wt/foreman-2ho commit a32dcba5 (foreman-auto ni818), based on pfh's fb2bd514. Deletion-local per-session single-flight guard in SessionManagerServiceLive following the existing DurableCommandQueue shape: winner runs the whole pipeline and publishes, overlapping callers await its Exit and report didDelete=false, and deleteSessionForClient returns immediately on false (no viewer switch, no session_deleted broadcast, no list rebroadcast, no log). RPC still returns {ok:true} -- settled from the contract, not taste: DeleteSession exposes no not-found result and the frontend discards the promise uncaught, so a rejection would surface as an unhandled rejection with no UX. HARD CONSTRAINT HELD: the no-route cleanup receipt is untouched and still fires for a genuine standalone delete; only the coalesced loser skips cleanup entirely, so it never enters the receipt path. Test D asserts this and its sensitivity was proven by temporarily suppressing the receipt and observing the failure. In-process guarding only, deliberately -- all production deletes originate in browser RPCs converging on the single per-project SessionManagerServiceLive and a restart destroys any losing caller. Root cause worth noting: the frontend fires deletion RPCs without awaiting or catching them from both the context-menu and bulk-delete paths, so this needed only a double-click. Committed 65557c16 on ds/phase-2a-button. ROOT CAUSE was not what the ticket's own framing implied. The four stories were not failing to settle within the 3s cap — quiescence detection was never watching them at all. waitForDomQuiescence awaited animation.finished for every running animation BEFORE installing its mutation observer, and all four stories render BlockGrid, whose pixel-cascade animations are infinite (style.css:165,185 via BlockGrid.svelte:56,72). An infinite animation's finished promise never resolves, so the observer was never installed, the wait always ran to its cap, and detection contributed nothing for exactly the stories that needed it. Reachable via ConnectOverlay's animated logo (ConnectOverlay.svelte:197), inherited by both ChatLayout captures, and SkillItem's running indicator (SkillItem.svelte:90). Same mechanism de3.20 traced for a comparable case. FIX: filter paused animations out of that wait, and freeze before the wait rather than after so the freeze is what pauses them. Cap, tolerance, workers and retries all unchanged, per the ticket's explicit prohibition on lengthening the wait. VERIFIED in-container under --platform linux/amd64, all three gates the acceptance criteria demanded: strict recapture 726 passed with ZERO baselines rewritten; strict rerun 726/726 (was 723/3) with ZERO 'did not quiesce' warnings (was the diagnostic signal for all four failures); non-strict CI-equivalent 726 passed / 0 flaky (was 725 passed / 1 flaky, so the retry CD was leaning on is gone). NOTE ON THE MECHANISM, because the implementing agent's headline explanation was wrong and the record should say so: it reported that freezing after the quiescence wait let the timeout frame decide the committed pixels. That cannot be right — pinning infinite animations to currentTime=0 changed ZERO captured pixels across all 726, so the injected animation-duration:0s CSS was already fixing the frame and timing was never selecting the content. The detection was broken, not the capture. The agent could not run any of the three gates itself (its sandbox denies the Docker socket) and correctly reported that rather than claiming success; the foreman ran all three.
